content.content:
1	# Frame Job graphics — the API
2	
3	A **graphic** is a motion graphic drawn by code: one JavaScript ES module
4	whose `render` returns an SVG string for each frame. Frame Job runs it in a
5	sandboxed QuickJS engine and rasterizes the SVG with resvg. The same frame
6	with the same props always draws the same pixels. A gradient is dithered
7	where it is rounded to 8 bits, by a fixed pattern of pixel position under
8	half a level, so dark gradients do not band; flat colours, images, text and
9	alpha are not. This page is the whole API. Every `js` block on it is run
10	by a test, so the examples work as written.
11	
12	## The module
13	
14	```js
15	export const meta = {
16	  name: "Lower third",        // shown in the inspector
17	  durationInFrames: 150,      // optional: the default length of a new clip
18	};
19	
20	export const schema = {
21	  title:    { type: "string",  default: "Jane Doe", label: "Title" },
22	  subtitle: { type: "string",  default: "Director of Photography" },
23	  accent:   { type: "color",   default: "#ff5a36" },
24	  size:     { type: "number",  default: 64, min: 12, max: 200, step: 1 },
25	  boxed:    { type: "boolean", default: true },
26	  align:    { type: "enum",    default: "left", options: ["left", "center", "right"] },
27	};
28	
29	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
30	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [-600, 96], { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
31	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [ctx.durationInFrames - 15, ctx.durationInFrames - 1], [1, 0],
32	    { clamp: true });
33	  const y = ctx.height - 200;
34	  return svg(ctx, `
35	    <g opacity="${fade}">
36	      ${props.boxed ? `<rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="700" height="150" fill="#101014"/>` : ""}
37	      <rect x="${x}" y="${y - 90}" width="12" height="150" fill="${props.accent}"/>
38	      <text x="${x + 40}" y="${y}" font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800"
39	            font-size="${props.size}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.title)}</text>
40	    </g>`);
41	}
42	```
43	
44	- `render(frame, props, ctx)` is required. It must return a string that
45	  starts with `<svg`; use `svg(ctx, body)` to write the root element.
46	- `meta` is optional (`{}` when absent). `name` and `durationInFrames` are
47	  read from it, and two keys only the Insert ▸ Graphic… dialog reads:
48	  `category`, the list the graphic is filed under (a string; "Other" when
49	  absent or blank), and `description`, one line shown under the dialog's
50	  preview. A module in the project's `graphics/` is listed under This
51	  Project whatever its `category`.
52	- `schema` is optional (`{}` when absent). It declares the props (below).
53	- The module is the only source of code: no `import`, no `eval`, no
54	  `Function`. The standard library below is already global.
55	- `frame` is an integer counted from the clip's first frame.
56	
57	## `ctx`
58	
59	| key | what |
60	|---|---|
61	| `fps` | the project's frame rate, e.g. `30` or `29.97002997` |
62	| `time` | `frame / fps`, in seconds |
63	| `durationInFrames` | the clip's length in frames |
64	| `progress` | `frame / max(1, durationInFrames - 1)`, clamped to 0–1 |
65	| `width`, `height` | the graphic's size in pixels |
66	| `canvas` | `{width, height}`, the project's canvas |
67	
68	Write every coordinate in terms of `ctx.width` and `ctx.height` (or a unit
69	such as `const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080`) so the graphic
70	draws at any size. That unit is the same as `ctx.height / 1080` on a
71	landscape canvas, and it keeps a portrait one from drawing 1.78 times too big.
72	
73	## The schema
74	
75	At most 64 keys. A key is letters, digits and `_`, starts with a letter or
76	`_`, and is at most 32 characters. Every entry needs a `type` and a
77	`default` of that type; `label` (else the key) and `help` (a tooltip) are
78	optional. Any entry may say `animate: false` (a boolean; absent is `true`):
79	an action never animates that prop, and the inspector writes it to the clip
80	even while an action is selected — for a count, a layout mode or a data
81	series a ramp would break.
82	
83	| `type` | value | options |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| `string` | text, at most 4096 characters | `multiline: true` for a text area |
86	| `number` | a finite number | `min`, `max`, `step` |
87	| `boolean` | `true` / `false` | |
88	| `color` | a CSS colour string: `"#ff5a36"`, `"rgb(255, 90, 54)"`, `"hsl(11, 100%, 61%)"`, `"tomato"` | |
89	| `enum` | one of `options` | `options`: 1–32 strings |
90	| `asset` | a file name in `graphics/assets/`, `null` or `""` (no image); `render` gets `null` for either of the last two | `kind: "image"` |
91	
92	A schema that breaks a rule does not compile, and the error says which rule.
93	A `color` entry's `default` must be a colour in the grammar
94	`interpolateColors` lists below, or the module does not compile:
95	`schema.accent.default "bluish" is not a color`. `props` receives the
96	default as written, not normalised.
97	`props` always has every schema key: a stored value replaces the default
98	only when it fits the type. A value that does not fit is a WARNING, the
99	default is drawn, and the frame still draws, e.g.
100	`props.size is a string but the schema says number; the default 64 is used`.
101	
102	## The standard library
103	
104	### `svg(ctx, body, {background})`
105	
106	The root element with the right `width`, `height` and `viewBox`.
107	
108	```js
109	const plain = svg(ctx, `<circle cx="100" cy="100" r="50" fill="#fff"/>`);
110	const onBlack = svg(ctx, "", { background: "#000000" });
111	```
112	
113	### `interpolate(value, input, output, {easing, clamp, extrapolateLeft, extrapolateRight})`
114	
115	Maps `value` through matching `input` and `output` ranges (two or more
116	points, `input` ascending). Outside `input` it extends the end segment
117	unless `clamp: true`; `extrapolateLeft` / `extrapolateRight` take
118	`"extend"`, `"clamp"` or `"identity"`.
119	
120	```js
121	const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 400], { clamp: true });
122	const pulse = interpolate(frame, [0, 15, 30], [1, 1.2, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutSine });
123	```
124	
125	### `Easing`
126	
127	`Easing.linear`, `Easing.bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)`, and `in`, `out` and `inOut`
128	of `quad`, `cubic`, `quart`, `expo`, `sine`, `back` and `elastic`, spelled
129	`Easing.inQuad`, `Easing.outCubic`, `Easing.inOutBack` and so on. Each takes
130	`t` in 0–1 and is exact at 0 and 1.
131	
132	```js
133	const eased = Easing.outCubic(0.5);
134	const custom = Easing.bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1)(0.5);
135	const y = interpolate(frame, [0, 20], [300, 0], { easing: Easing.outBack, clamp: true });
136	```
137	
138	### `spring({frame, fps, stiffness = 100, damping = 10, mass = 1, from = 0, to = 1})`
139	
140	A physical spring from `from` to `to`, starting at frame 0 (use
141	`frame - delay` to start later). It overshoots unless damped. The same frame
142	always answers the same value.
143	
144	```js
145	const scale = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 14 });
146	const late = spring({ frame: frame - 12, fps: ctx.fps, stiffness: 180, from: 0.5, to: 1 });
147	```
148	
149	### `interpolateColors(value, input, colors)`
150	
151	Blends colours in OKLab and answers `#rrggbb` (or `#rrggbbaa` when a colour
152	has alpha). Clamped outside `input`. A colour is `#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`,
153	`#rrggbbaa`, `rgb()` / `rgba()` (channels 0–255 or a percentage, alpha 0–1
154	or a percentage), `hsl()` / `hsla()` (hue in degrees, saturation and
155	lightness percentages), or one of the 147 CSS colour names or
156	`transparent` — the same colours a `color` prop takes. A value out of range
157	(`rgb(300, 0, 0)`) throws rather than being clamped.
158	
159	```js
160	const fill = interpolateColors(frame, [0, 60], ["#ff5a36", "#3666ff"]);
161	const glass = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["rgba(255, 255, 255, 0)", "#ffffff"]);
162	const sky = interpolateColors(ctx.progress, [0, 1], ["hsl(200, 80%, 30%)", "skyblue"]);
163	```
164	
165	### `random(seed)`
166	
167	A number in [0, 1) that depends only on `seed` (a number or a string).
168	`Math.random` does not exist in a graphic; this replaces it.
169	
170	```js
171	const jitter = random(`dot-${frame}`) * 10;
172	const hue = Math.floor(random(42) * 360);
173	```
174	
175	### `noise2D(seed, x, y)` and `noise3D(seed, x, y, z)`
176	
177	Simplex noise in about −1..1. Use `noise3D` with time as the third axis for
178	smooth drift.
179	
180	```js
181	const drift = noise2D("wave", frame / 60, 0) * 40;
182	const wobble = noise3D(7, 0.5, 0.5, ctx.time) * 20;
183	```
184	
185	### Paths: `getLength(d)`, `getPointAtLength(d, length)` and `evolvePath(progress, d)`
186	
187	`d` is SVG path data: every command (`M L H V C S Q T A Z`) and its
188	relative form. `getLength` answers the path's length, curves and arcs
189	measured to within about 0.01 %. `getPointAtLength` answers `{x, y, angle}`:
190	the point that far along the path (`length` is clamped to the path) and the
191	way the path is heading there, in degrees, ready for `rotate()`.
192	`evolvePath` answers `{strokeDasharray, strokeDashoffset}` for a `progress`
193	of 0–1: put both on the `<path>` and it is drawn from its start up to that
194	fraction. Its dash is 0.1 % longer than the measured length, so a closed
195	outline closes at 1.
196	
197	A path of several pieces (more than one `M`) draws them all at once, each
198	from its own start and at the same speed, the longest finishing at 1; pieces
199	drawn one after another are one `<path>` each. A path that cannot be read
200	throws, naming where reading stopped —
201	`getLength: cannot parse the path at character 6: "X 5 5"` — and is never a
202	silent zero. A number too large to do arithmetic with (`1e999`, or a line
203	1e200 long, whose square overflows) is refused in the same sentence, so no
204	answer is ever `Infinity` or `NaN`.
205	
206	The paths a graphic measures are remembered, so the same `d` costs a lookup
207	on later calls and frames — up to 32 paths, and about 50,000 characters and
208	measured pieces between them (a curve is 64 pieces). Past either limit all
209	are forgotten and measured again when next asked for, so with paths that
210	large take every length and point from one before turning to the next.
211	
212	```js
213	const d = `M 200 ${ctx.height / 2} C 600 100 1000 900 1400 ${ctx.height / 2}`;
214	const total = getLength(d);
215	const tip = getPointAtLength(d, total * ctx.progress);
216	const dash = evolvePath(ctx.progress, d);
217	const line = `<path d="${d}" fill="none" stroke="#ffffff" stroke-width="8"
218	  stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
219	  <circle cx="${tip.x}" cy="${tip.y}" r="12" fill="#ffcc00"/>`;
220	```
221	
222	### `measureText(text, font)`
223	
224	`font` is `{family, size, weight, style, letterSpacing, xmlSpace}`
225	(defaults Montserrat, 16, 400, `"normal"`, 0, `"default"`). Answers
226	`{width, ascent, descent, lineHeight, inkX, inkWidth}`: `width` is the
227	advance (where the next word starts); `inkX` / `inkWidth` are the drawn
228	glyphs. With `xmlSpace: "default"` runs of spaces collapse as SVG draws
229	them; with `"preserve"` a run of spaces beside a drawn glyph counts, as
230	`xml:space="preserve"` draws it, and any other value throws. Text that is
231	only whitespace measures zero either way. A family that is not installed
232	throws, naming the families that are.
233	
234	```js
235	const m = measureText("Hello", { family: "Montserrat", size: 64, weight: 800 });
236	const boxWidth = m.width + 80;
237	const gap = measureText("a  b", { family: "sans-serif", size: 48, xmlSpace: "preserve" });
238	```
239	
240	### `wrapText(text, maxWidth, font)`
241	
242	Lines that each fit `maxWidth`; a word longer than the width breaks by
243	characters.
244	
245	```js
246	const lines = wrapText("A title long enough to need two lines", 600,
247	  { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 64, weight: 700 });
248	```
249	
250	### `fitText(text, maxWidth, font, {min = 8, max = 400})`
251	
252	The largest whole font size at which `text` fits `maxWidth` on one line.
253	
254	```js
255	const size = fitText("BREAKING", ctx.width - 200, { family: "Anton" }, { max: 300 });
256	```
257	
258	### `textLines(lines, {x, y, lineHeight, anchor, fill, font})`
259	
260	A `<text>` with one `<tspan>` per line, the family QUOTED for you (a CSS
261	generic such as `sans-serif` is written bare, as it must be).
262	`anchor` is `"start"`, `"middle"` or `"end"`; `lineHeight` defaults to
263	1.2 × the size. A font with `xmlSpace: "preserve"` writes
264	`xml:space="preserve"` on the `<text>`, so it draws the spaces `measureText`
265	counted; a `style` of `"italic"` or `"oblique"` and a non-zero
266	`letterSpacing` are written as `font-style` and `letter-spacing`, so it draws
267	the font `wrapText` broke the lines with.
268	
269	```js
270	const font = { family: "Source Sans 3", size: 48, weight: 600 };
271	const body = textLines(wrapText("Two short lines of text", 400, font),
272	  { x: 100, y: 200, anchor: "start", fill: "#ffffff", font });
273	const code = textLines(["let  x = 1;"],
274	  { x: 100, y: 300, font: { family: "monospace", size: 32, xmlSpace: "preserve" } });
275	```
276	
277	### `escapeXml(s)`
278	
279	Escapes `& < > " '` — put every prop you write into markup through it.
280	
281	```js
282	const safe = escapeXml("Tom & Jerry <live>");
283	```
284	
285	### `formatNumber(n, {decimals = 0, separator = ","})`
286	
287	There is no `Intl` in the engine; this groups thousands.
288	
289	```js
290	const label = formatNumber(1234567.891, { decimals: 2 });
291	const plain = formatNumber(Math.round(interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, 5000], { clamp: true })));
292	```
293	
294	### `asset(name)`
295	
296	The href for a file in the project's `graphics/assets/` folder, for
297	`<image href="…">`. A name that is not there is a warning naming the files
298	that are; the image then does not draw.
299	
300	An asset's name must not start with `.` or `#`, must hold none of
301	`/ : " ' < > &` and no control character, and is at most 247 bytes. A
302	picture added under any other name is renamed as it is copied in —
303	`#logo&mark.png` becomes `logo-mark.png`, then `logo-mark-2.png` if that is
304	taken — and you are told the name to use. A file put in the folder by hand
305	under such a name is skipped, with a warning.
306	
307	```js
308	const logo = `<image href="${asset("logo.png")}" x="40" y="40" width="200" height="200"/>`;
309	```

311	## Fonts
312	
313	A graphic draws with the fonts bundled with Frame Job, plus any `.ttf` /
314	`.otf` in the project's `graphics/fonts/`. Never the system's.
315	
316	| family | weights |
317	|---|---|
318	| Anton | 400 |
319	| Bebas Neue | 400 |
320	| Darker Grotesque | variable, 300–900 |
321	| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
322	| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
323	| Source Sans 3 | variable, 200–900 |
324	| Source Serif 4 | variable, 200–900 |
325	
326	The CSS generic families draw in bundled faces: `serif` is Source Serif 4,
327	`sans-serif` is Source Sans 3 and `monospace` is IBM Plex Mono. Write a
328	generic unquoted (`font-family="sans-serif"`); quoted, it names a family
329	called "sans-serif", which is not installed. `cursive` and `fantasy` are not
330	installed.
331	
332	**Quote a family** in `font-family` or the `font` shorthand when any word
333	of it starts with a digit: `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`,
334	`font: 48px 'Source Sans 3'`. Unquoted, `Source Sans 3` is not a
335	valid family list: it draws nothing, with a warning. `textLines` quotes
336	for you. A family the set lacks draws nothing, with a warning naming the
337	families that are installed; in a list (`"Nope, Montserrat"`) the first
338	installed family draws.
339	
340	## The sandbox
341	
342	A graphic is a pure function of `frame`, `props`, `ctx` and its fonts and
343	assets. These refuse, with these sentences:
344	
345	```text
346	Math.random()        → Math.random is not available; use random(seed)
347	import x from "x"    → imports are not available in a graphic; the standard library is global
348	new Function("…")    → Function is not available in a graphic; the module is the one source of code
349	eval("…")            → ReferenceError: eval is not defined
350	```
351	
352	`Date` is frozen: `Date.now()` is `946684800000` and `new Date()` is
353	2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. There is no `fetch`, file, clock, `performance`,
354	`WebAssembly` or `Intl`. Modern syntax works: template literals, `??`, `?.`,
355	`**`, destructuring, `Array.prototype.at`, `replaceAll`, `findLast`.
356	
357	## Limits
358	
359	- **Time**: each call has a budget — 250 ms per frame in preview, 2 s in an
360	  export. The module's top level has one too. Over it, the answer is an
361	  error such as `over the 250 ms budget at frame 12 (InternalError:
362	  interrupted)`.
363	- **Memory**: 64 MB of heap and 1 MB of stack per engine. Past either is an
364	  error with a line and column.
365	- **Size**: a graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
366	- **The answer**: `render` must return an SVG string. `undefined` is
367	  ``render returned undefined at frame 12 — did you forget `return`?``.
368	  The string may be at most 8 MiB (8388608 bytes); a longer one is
369	  `render returned 9000000 bytes at frame 12; the SVG may be at most
370	  8388608 bytes`.
371	
372	## Diagnostics
373	
374	Every problem comes back as `{level, message, line, column, frame}`.
375	`level` is `"error"` (nothing drew) or `"warning"` (it drew anyway).
376	`line` and `column` are the module's own, when known; for a timeout they
377	are where the function begins, not the statement that ran long. `frame` is
378	set for a problem found while drawing. A warning from the module's top level
379	(such as `asset("x")` outside `render`) has no frame, and comes back with the
380	module's compile: `ok` is still `true`.
381	
382	## Working over MCP
383	
384	Read `graphic_reference` once. `write_graphic {name, source}` answers `ok` and
385	`diagnostics`: write again until `ok` is true. `render_graphic {name, frames}`
386	draws up to 16 frames on a contact sheet with no clip, at most 134217728
387	pixels of frames in all (two at 8192×8192, or sixteen at 3840×2160);
388	`add_graphic_clip {name}` places it, `render_frame` shows a frame,
389	`set_graphic {patch: {props}}` changes it.
390	`paste_attributes {clips, payload, groups: ["graphic"]}` copies one clip's props onto other clips
391	drawn by the same module. `import_graphic_font {path}` answers `families`, the exact names
392	`font-family` must say; `import_graphic_asset {path}` adds a picture for
393	`asset(name)`; its `name` is the one to use, and `renamed_from` says it was
394	renamed. `get_graphic` reads a module or names the folder, which your file
395	tools may edit too; its `API.md` is this page, `API.d.ts` its types.
396	`get_graphic {}`'s `warnings` says what the folder's scan skipped or could
397	not watch, such as a file whose name is not a module name. The app keeps the
398	last 10 texts of each module whenever it sees one replaced: `kept`, in
399	`write_graphic`'s and `get_graphic {name}`'s answers, lists their revisions,
400	newest first, and `get_graphic {}`'s `history` lists every name with a kept
401	text, deleted modules included. `restore_graphic {name, revision?}` writes a
402	kept text back (the newest by default) and keeps the one it replaced.
403	`delete_graphic {name}` removes a module no clip draws and keeps its text, so
404	`restore_graphic` brings it back. `rename_graphic {name, to}` renames a
405	module and repoints every clip that draws it as one undo step; undo renames
406	the file back. The folder's `history/` is the app's: leave it to those three
407	tools. A successful
408	`export` answers `graphic_warnings`, each distinct warning a graphic gave
409	while the file was drawn, with its name and frame.

411	## Animating a prop from the timeline
412	
413	A graphic clip's props can be the target of an action, as a clip's position or opacity can:
414	`add_action {clip, at, duration}` makes the span, and `set_action_end {clip, action, patch:
415	{graphic: {props: {…}}}}` names the values the props end at. Each value is checked against your
416	schema as `set_graphic` checks it, `min` and `max` included, using the module as it is now. Across
417	the action a `number` and a `color` ramp along its curve, a `color` in OKLab, giving the same middle
418	`interpolateColors` gives; a `string`, `boolean` and `enum` change to the end's value when the
419	action ends, and an `asset` changes to the end's image when the action ends, `""` naming no image
420	there (a `null` stops animating the prop); a prop whose entry says `animate: false` cannot be
421	animated (`set_action_end` refuses a value for it). A prop the clip holds no value
422	for starts from the schema's `default` as it is when an action first names it, and that value is
423	written into the clip, so a later change to the default does not move the animation; an asset
424	whose default is `null` starts from `""`. `render` gets
425	that frame's values every frame, and your own animation from `frame` still runs on top. A `null`
426	for a prop in `set_action_end`'s patch stops animating it.
427	
428	**An animated number arrives with decimals**: 64 to 129 is 96.5 halfway, never rounded and never
429	snapped to `step`. A module that needs a whole number rounds it itself, or marks the prop
430	`animate: false` so no action ramps it. One that does neither —
431	`new Array(props.count)` is the usual case — throws on a fraction, so those frames draw the error
432	card, and an export stops there.
433	
434	```js
435	export const meta = { name: "Bars", durationInFrames: 90 };
436	export const schema = {
437	  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1 },
438	  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" },
439	};
440	
441	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
442	  const n = Math.round(props.count);
443	  const w = ctx.width / (2 * n);
444	  let bars = "";
445	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
446	    bars += `<rect x="${(2 * i + 0.5) * w}" y="${ctx.height / 3}" width="${w}"
447	      height="${ctx.height / 3}" fill="${props.accent}"/>`;
448	  }
449	  return svg(ctx, bars);
450	}
451	```
452	
453	A colour blends in OKLab with straight alpha, exactly as `interpolateColors` blends it: `#ff0000`
454	to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, not the muddy `#800080` of a channel-by-channel blend, and
455	`#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, grey and half transparent. While a prop
456	moves, every frame is drawn anew, so a graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the
457	length of the action.
458	
459	## Video inside a graphic: the matte
460	
461	A graphic cannot read a video's pixels. To show video inside a shape the graphic draws, put the
462	graphic on the track directly above the video and switch that track to a **matte**: Track ▸ Matte
463	in the app, or `set_track {track, matte}` over MCP. A matte track's clips are never drawn. What
464	they show cuts the track directly behind: with `alpha`, the video shows where the graphic is
465	opaque; with `alpha_inverted`, where it is transparent; with `luma` and `luma_inverted`, by the
466	brightness of what it draws. `matte: "none"` turns it off. Where the matte track has no clip, the
467	video shows uncut. The module is written and called exactly as anywhere else. Fill the window in
468	white so it works in every mode, and animate it as usual: the cut follows each frame.
469	
470	```js
471	export const meta = { name: "Window", durationInFrames: 90 };
472	export const schema = { radius: { type: "number", default: 24, min: 0, max: 200 } };
473	
474	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
475	  const t = spring({ frame, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 18 });
476	  const w = ctx.width * 0.6 * t;
477	  const h = ctx.height * 0.6 * t;
478	  return svg(ctx, `<rect x="${(ctx.width - w) / 2}" y="${(ctx.height - h) / 2}"
479	    width="${w}" height="${h}" rx="${props.radius}" fill="#ffffff"/>`);
480	}
481	```
482	
483	On a matte track a clip's position, scale, opacity, crop and actions still shape the window. Its
484	blend mode, drop shadow and reflection do nothing. The matted video's own drop shadow follows the
485	cut-out shape.
486	
487	## Idioms
488	
489	### A slide-in
490	
491	```js
492	export const meta = { name: "Slide in", durationInFrames: 90 };
493	export const schema = { text: { type: "string", default: "Hello" } };
494	
495	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
496	  const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
497	  const x = interpolate(frame, [0, 18], [-ctx.width / 2, ctx.width / 2],
498	    { easing: Easing.outCubic, clamp: true });
499	  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${x}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
500	    font-family="Montserrat" font-weight="800" font-size="${120 * u}"
501	    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(props.text)}</text>`);
502	}
503	```
504	
505	### A staggered list
506	
507	```js
508	export const meta = { name: "Agenda" };
509	export const schema = {
510	  items: { type: "string", default: "Intro\nDemo\nQuestions", multiline: true, animate: false },
511	  accent: { type: "color", default: "#ffcc00" },
512	};
513	
514	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
515	  const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
516	  const rows = props.items.split("\n").filter((s) => s.trim()).map((item, i) => {
517	    const t = spring({ frame: frame - i * 6, fps: ctx.fps, damping: 16 });
518	    const y = 300 * u + i * 110 * u;
519	    return `<g opacity="${Math.min(1, t)}" transform="translate(${(1 - t) * 80 * u} 0)">
520	      <rect x="${160 * u}" y="${y - 50 * u}" width="${14 * u}" height="${64 * u}" fill="${props.accent}"/>
521	      <text x="${200 * u}" y="${y}" font-family="'Source Sans 3'" font-weight="600"
522	        font-size="${64 * u}" fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(item)}</text></g>`;
523	  });
524	  return svg(ctx, rows.join(""));
525	}
526	```
527	
528	### A counter
529	
530	```js
531	export const meta = { name: "Counter", durationInFrames: 120 };
532	export const schema = {
533	  to: { type: "number", default: 25000, min: 0 },
534	  suffix: { type: "string", default: " views" },
535	};
536	
537	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
538	  const value = interpolate(frame, [0, 60], [0, props.to], { easing: Easing.outExpo, clamp: true });
539	  const text = formatNumber(Math.round(value)) + props.suffix;
540	  return svg(ctx, `<text x="${ctx.width / 2}" y="${ctx.height / 2}" text-anchor="middle"
541	    font-family="'IBM Plex Mono'" font-weight="500" font-size="${ctx.height / 8}"
542	    fill="#ffffff">${escapeXml(text)}</text>`);
543	}
544	```
545	
546	### Fit and wrap a title
547	
548	```js
549	export const meta = { name: "Title card" };
550	export const schema = {
551	  title: { type: "string", default: "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog" },
552	};
553	
554	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
555	  const maxWidth = ctx.width * 0.8;
556	  const base = { family: "Bebas Neue", weight: 400 };
557	  const size = fitText(props.title, maxWidth * 2, base, { min: 48, max: 220 });
558	  const font = Object.assign({}, base, { size });
559	  const lines = wrapText(props.title, maxWidth, font);
560	  const top = ctx.height / 2 - (lines.length - 1) * size * 0.6;
561	  const fade = interpolate(frame, [0, 12], [0, 1], { clamp: true });
562	  return svg(ctx, `<g opacity="${fade}">${textLines(lines,
563	    { x: ctx.width / 2, y: top, anchor: "middle", fill: "#ffffff", font })}</g>`,
564	    { background: "#16161a" });
565	}
566	```
567	
568	### A draw-on stroke
569	
570	`evolvePath` measures the path and answers the dash that draws it up to a
571	progress of 0–1.
572	
573	```js
574	export const meta = { name: "Underline", durationInFrames: 60 };
575	export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ff5a36" } };
576	
577	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
578	  const y = ctx.height * 0.62;
579	  const d = `M ${ctx.width * 0.2} ${y} q ${ctx.width * 0.3} ${ctx.height * 0.05} ${ctx.width * 0.6} 0`;
580	  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 24], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
581	  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
582	  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}"
583	    stroke-width="${ctx.height / 90}" stroke-linecap="round" fill="none"
584	    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>`);
585	}
586	```
587	
588	### Follow a path
589	
590	`getPointAtLength` answers where the path is and which way it is heading;
591	`rotate(angle)` turns an arrowhead drawn pointing right to match.
592	
593	```js
594	export const meta = { name: "Arrow", durationInFrames: 60 };
595	export const schema = { color: { type: "color", default: "#ffffff" } };
596	
597	export function render(frame, props, ctx) {
598	  const w = ctx.width;
599	  const h = ctx.height;
600	  const d = `M ${w * 0.2} ${h * 0.7} C ${w * 0.4} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.6} ${h * 0.2} ${w * 0.8} ${h * 0.5}`;
601	  const drawn = interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 1], { easing: Easing.inOutCubic, clamp: true });
602	  const dash = evolvePath(drawn, d);
603	  const tip = getPointAtLength(d, getLength(d) * drawn);
604	  const s = h / 36;
605	  return svg(ctx, `<path d="${d}" stroke="${props.color}" stroke-width="${h / 120}" fill="none"
606	    stroke-dasharray="${dash.strokeDasharray}" stroke-dashoffset="${dash.strokeDashoffset}"/>
607	    <path d="M ${-s} ${-s * 0.6} L ${s * 0.5} 0 L ${-s} ${s * 0.6} Z" fill="${props.color}"
608	    transform="translate(${tip.x} ${tip.y}) rotate(${tip.angle})"/>`);
609	}
610	```
611	# graphic/CLAUDE.md — the graphics engine's rules
612	
613	Applies to everything under `graphic/`, the crate that draws a graphic clip
614	(road map 10: `designs/adr/roadmap-10-graphics.md`; the full design is
615	`archive/roadmap-10.md` §5a). Build commands are the root
616	`CLAUDE.md`'s: `make test` and `make lint` run this crate after the core.
617	The crate's record is road map 10 §10.4.
618	
619	## Module map
620	
621	- `lib.rs` — `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, module declarations and re-exports
622	  only. No implementation code.
623	- `diagnostic.rs` — `Level`, `Diagnostic` (`{level, message, line, column,
624	  frame}`, §5b) and its JSON, keys in that order.
625	- `images.rs` — the decoded-image cache (spec §11 G-39, #127): `Asset
626	  {data, digest}`, a process-wide `Mutex` map from an asset's own SHA-256
627	  to `Ready`/`Building`/`Refused`/`Skipped {len}`, `set_image_cache_limit`,
628	  `image_cache_bytes`, the doc-hidden `image_cache_builds`, `cached_kind`,
629	  and the builder of a stored-deflate RGBA8 PNG copy, used only when it
630	  decodes to exactly the original's pixmap and `imagesize` reads the same
631	  size. No lock is held across a decode, an encode or a usvg call; a
632	  build writes only while its digest is still `Building`; the default limit
633	  is 0, so a binary that sets none takes the original route. The doc-hidden
634	  `set_image_build_hook` installs an `ImageBuildHook` every build calls
635	  between its two locks with none held, so a test can hold a build there.
636	- `library.rs` — `Library`: the font set (`fontdb`, from bytes, never
637	  `load_system_fonts`, G-6) and the asset map (each asset keeps its own
638	  SHA-256; a PNG or JPEG kind is asked of the cache first), their content `version`
639	  (SHA-256 with length prefixes), the `measure_text` memo, and the
640	  crate-private `options()` builder whose resolvers record into a `Probe`
641	  what resvg never reports. It also keeps the face-ID → font-blob map and
642	  the usage set (`Usage`, `Library::usage()`, spec §11 G-46), filled by
643	  `select_font`, the wrapped fallback selector and `resolve_string` (image
644	  kinds only); each closure calls usvg FIRST and only then locks the usage
645	  set for its own insert, because a nested SVG asset re-enters on the same
646	  thread. The generic families map to bundled faces
647	  (`serif` Source Serif 4, `sans-serif` Source Sans 3, `monospace` IBM Plex
648	  Mono, G-6), and `select_font` queries only the text's own families,
649	  never usvg's appended serif fallback, so a missing family still draws
650	  nothing and is warned.
651	- `raster.rs` — `rasterize`, `MAX_SIDE`, the RGBA→BGRA row copy into the
652	  caller's strided buffer, and every warning text `rasterize` answers:
653	  missing family, unparseable `font-family` (the scan of attributes, `style`
654	  attributes and `<style>` sheets, and the family of a `font` shorthand in
655	  a `style` attribute or sheet), unknown href, data: URL, non-image
656	  asset, size mismatch. The texts are load-bearing: tests match them and
657	  the app shows them on the clip.
658	- `measure.rs` — `FontStyle`, `TextFont` (with `preserve_space`, the
659	  `xmlSpace` key, G-22), `TextMetrics`, `measure_text`; a generic family
660	  is written unquoted.
661	- `module.rs` — `Module` (`Send + Sync + Clone`, holds no QuickJS object):
662	  `compile`, the SHA-256 revision (G-13), `meta`/`schema` read through
663	  `JSON.stringify` in the module's key order (`{}` when not exported),
664	  `defaults()`, its top-level warnings (`warnings()`, G-21 (b)).
665	- `runtime.rs` — `Engine` (one QuickJS `Runtime` + `Context` per (thread,
666	  module), §5b's limits, the interrupt deadline), the `thread_local!` map
667	  swept by `Weak` before each call, at most `ENGINES_PER_THREAD` (16, spec
668	  §11 G-21) engines with the least recently used evicted after the call,
669	  `svg`, `Engine::parse_colours` (the stdlib's `__parseColour` per text
670	  under one deadline, storing nothing; G-25), `engine_count`, `HEAP_BYTES`,
671	  `STACK_BYTES`, `SVG_BYTES` (8 MiB, spec §11 G-20 (c)). The crate's one
672	  clock.
673	- `sandbox.rs` — the sandbox script (G-5) and the loader that resolves no
674	  specifier, with `IMPORT_REFUSAL`.
675	- `exception.rs` — QuickJS error → Diagnostic: `{name}: {message}`, the
676	  position from `stack` (the module's own frame first), the budget's
677	  sentences, what `render` returned (a string over `SVG_BYTES` refused by its
678	  length, before the `<svg` check). The texts are load-bearing.
679	- `host.rs` — the globals `__measureText`, `__assetNames`, `__warn` and
680	  `__namedColour` (svgtypes' named-colour table for the stdlib's colour
681	  parser).
682	- `props.rs` — `check_schema` (compile, strict; it takes a colour reader,
683	  which `Module::compile` builds from `Engine::parse_colours` over the
684	  schema's colour defaults, G-25 (a); a non-boolean `animate` on an entry
685	  is refused, G-41), `overlay` (render,
686	  lenient; every surprise a warning; an asset stored as `""` is handed to
687	  `render` as `null`, silently, G-42) and the schema's limits `MAX_PROPS`,
688	  `MAX_OPTIONS`, `MAX_STRING` and `TYPES`, which the core restates as
689	  `GRAPHIC_<X>` (`core/tests/graphic_ffi.rs` pins each pair;
690	  `tests/reference.rs` pins the numbers the reference states, and its
691	  typings' key cap).
692	- `stdlib.js`, `noise.js`, `path.js` — §5c's standard library, evaluated

542	        guard names.count == 1, let name = names.first else { return nil }

593	    /// included, G-41), each asset popup's names (the selected end's

599	        guard allGraphic else { return super.structureSignature + "|-" }
600	        let shared = self.shared()

602	        let keys = parsed?.schema.entries.map { String(describing: $0) } ?? []
603	        let stale = GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: storedProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
604	        var messages = ["-", "-"]

626	    private func assetSignature(_ schema: GraphicSchema?) -> String {

636	    /// One row per schema key in the module's order, then the stale keys,
637	    /// sorted, then — with an action selected — the end's own stale keys
638	    /// (G-34 (l), O2), a declared key whose entry is not `animatable` among
639	    /// them (G-41 (c)). With no compiled schema every stored key is stale.
640	    /// Reset nulls every stored key; with an action selected it writes each
641	    /// declared default through the rows' own split, into the END (an
642	    /// asset's `null` as `""`, G-42 (d)), an `animate: false` prop's (G-41
643	    /// (d)) onto the clip (O7). Its `differs` folds from the rows.
644	    func propertiesSection() -> InspectorSection {
645	        let binding = self.binding
646	        let shared = self.shared()
647	        let parsed = schema(shared)
648	        let clips = { binding.graphicClips }
649	        let assets = { [weak self] in self?.assetNames() ?? [] }
650	        var rows: [NSView] = parsed?.schema.entries.map {
651	            GraphicSchemaRows.row(
652	                $0, binding, clips: clips, schema: parsed?.raw ?? [:], assets: assets)
653	        } ?? []
654	        let stored = storedProps()
655	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: stored, schema: parsed?.schema) {
656	            rows.append(
657	                GraphicSchemaRows.staleRow(
658	                    key: key, value: stored[key] ?? .null, binding, clips: clips))
659	        }
660	        let ends = endProps()
661	        let declared = Set(parsed?.schema.keys ?? [])
662	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: ends, schema: parsed?.schema) {
663	            rows.append(
664	                GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleRow(
665	                    key: key, value: ends[key] ?? .null, declared: declared.contains(key), binding))
666	        }
667	        let note: String?
668	        if parsed == nil {
669	            note = "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below."
670	        } else if parsed?.schema.entries.isEmpty == true {
671	            note = "The module declares no properties."
672	        } else {
673	            note = nil
674	        }
675	        let count = parsed?.schema.entries.count ?? 0
676	        return InspectorSection(
677	            id: "graphic.properties", title: "Properties",
678	            summary: { count == 1 ? "1 property" : "\(count) properties" },
679	            note: note.map { text -> () -> String? in { text } },
680	            reset: {
681	                if binding.selectedAction != nil {
682	                    let entries = parsed?.schema.entries ?? []
683	                    let defaults = Dictionary(
684	                        entries.map { ($0.key, $0.default) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
685	                    binding.apply(
686	                        "Reset Graphic Properties",
687	                        binding.ops(
688	                            graphic: defaults, entries: entries, clips: clips(), schema: parsed?.raw))
689	                    return
690	                }
691	                let targets = clips()
692	                var keys = Set<String>()
693	                for clip in targets { keys.formUnion(clip.graphic?.props.keys.map { $0 } ?? []) }
694	                guard !keys.isEmpty else { return NSSound.beep() }
695	                binding.apply(
696	                    "Reset Graphic Properties",
697	                    [GraphicSchemaRows.op(
698	                        clips: targets,
699	                        props: Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: keys.map { ($0, NSNull()) }),
700	                        schema: parsed?.raw)])
701	            },
702	            defaultExpanded: true,
703	            rows: rows)
704	    }

803	// buttons (Open in Editor, Reveal in Finder, Duplicate as New Graphic…), and
804	// what the module says about the clip, each group under its own heading
805	// (#221): "Compiling the module" over its compile (an error, or what its top
806	// level warned), when there is any; the clip's FIRST frame drawn and
807	// rasterized at the clip's own size, when one was drawn, so a missing font
808	// or a size mismatch shows here (G3c's owed warning, road map 10 §10.6); and
809	// "In the graphics folder" over what the folder's scan skipped or could not
810	// watch, each with Reveal (G-24 (b)).
811	//
812	// **The report is the paused frame's own two calls** — `module.svg` then
813	// `library.rasterize` at `graphic.width × height`
814	// (`LayerRenderersGraphic.swift`) — memoised by module, revision, library,
815	// the recipe's frame hash and the size, so a miss costs one paused frame.
816	// While a live gesture runs nothing is recomputed: a miss answers the
817	// clip's last report.

821	/// What a graphic clip's module says about it: its compile's diagnostics,
822	/// and the first frame's — drawn at the graphic's `frame`.
823	struct GraphicClipReport: Equatable {
824	    let compile: [GraphicDiagnostic]
825	    let render: [GraphicDiagnostic]
826	    let frame: Int?
827	
828	    static let empty = GraphicClipReport(compile: [], render: [], frame: nil)
829	}

843	                    InspectorNoteLabel { "Select one module's clips to edit its properties." },
844	                ])

846	        let current = { [weak self] in self?.shared() }
847	        func metaName() -> String {
848	            if case .compiled(_, _, let meta, _)? = current()?.entry,
849	               let name = meta["name"] as? String, !name.isEmpty
850	            {

858	        }
859	        let open: () -> Void = { [weak self] in self?.openFile() }
860	        let hasFile = { current()?.file != nil }
861	        let duplicate = OptionButtonControl(
862	            title: "Duplicate as New Graphic…",
863	            action: { [weak self] in
864	                guard let self, let shared = current(), let file = shared.file else {
865	                    return NSSound.beep()
866	                }
867	                self.duplicateAsNewGraphic(file, schema: self.schema(shared)?.raw)
868	            },
869	            enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {})
870	        var rows: [NSView] = [
871	            inspectorRow("Name", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { metaName() }]),
872	            inspectorRow("File", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { "\(first.name).js" }]),
873	            inspectorRow("Revision", [inspectorReadout(width: 170) { revision() }]),
874	            inspectorButtonRow([
875	                OptionButtonControl(
876	                    title: "Open in Editor", action: open, enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {}),
877	                OptionButtonControl(
878	                    title: "Reveal in Finder",
879	                    action: {
880	                        guard let url = current()?.file?.url else { return NSSound.beep() }
881	                        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])
882	                    },
883	                    enabled: hasFile, onEdit: {}),
884	            ]),
885	            inspectorButtonRow([duplicate]),
886	        ]
887	        var report = GraphicClipReport.empty
888	        if let clip = binding.graphicClips.first, let document = binding.document {
889	            let version = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)?.libraryVersion
890	            report = self.report(for: clip, first, libraryVersion: version ?? "")
891	        }
892	        let diagnostics = report.compile + report.render
893	        if !report.compile.isEmpty {
894	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { "Compiling the module" })
895	            rows += report.compile.map { GraphicDiagnosticRow($0, onOpen: open) }
896	        }
897	        if report.frame != nil {
898	            let checked = report.render.isEmpty
899	                ? "No errors or warnings at the clip's first frame"
900	                : "Checked at the clip's first frame"
901	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { checked })
902	            rows += report.render.map { GraphicDiagnosticRow($0, onOpen: open) }
903	        }
904	        let folder = folderWarnings()
905	        if !folder.isEmpty {
906	            let reveal: () -> Void = { [weak self] in
907	                guard let url = self?.binding.document?.graphicStore?.folderURL,
908	                      FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: url.path)
909	                else { return NSSound.beep() }
910	                NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])
911	            }
912	            rows.append(InspectorNoteLabel { "In the graphics folder" })
913	            rows += folder.map {
914	                GraphicDiagnosticRow(
915	                    GraphicDiagnostic(
916	                        level: "warning", message: $0, line: nil, column: nil, frame: nil),
917	                    openTitle: "Reveal", help: "Reveal the graphics folder in Finder",
918	                    onOpen: reveal)
919	            }
920	        }
921	        let errors = diagnostics.filter { $0.level == "error" }.count
922	        let warnings = diagnostics.count - errors + folder.count
923	        return InspectorSection(
924	            id: "graphic.source", title: "Source",
925	            summary: {
926	                errors > 0 ? (errors == 1 ? "1 error" : "\(errors) errors")
927	                    : warnings > 0 ? (warnings == 1 ? "1 warning" : "\(warnings) warnings")
928	                    : metaName()
929	            },
930	            defaultExpanded: false,
931	            rows: rows)
932	    }
933	
934	    /// Opens the shared module's file in the app the system gives `.js`.
935	    func openFile() {
936	        guard let url = shared()?.file?.url else { return NSSound.beep() }
937	        NSWorkspace.shared.open(url)
938	    }
939	
940	    /// The module's compile, and `clip`'s first frame drawn and rasterized at
941	    /// the clip's own size — through the memo, and never recomputed while a
942	    /// live gesture runs.
943	    func report(
944	        for clip: ClipSnapshot, _ shared: Shared, libraryVersion: String
945	    ) -> GraphicClipReport {
946	        let module: GraphicModule, revision: String
947	        switch shared.entry {
948	        case nil:
949	            return GraphicClipReport(
950	                compile: [GraphicDiagnostic.noModule(shared.name)],
951	                render: [], frame: nil)
952	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
953	            return GraphicClipReport(compile: diagnostics, render: [], frame: nil)
954	        case .compiled(let compiled, let hash, _, _)?:
955	            module = compiled
956	            revision = hash
957	        }
958	        guard let graphic = clip.graphic, let document = binding.document else { return .empty }
959	        if document.isLiveEditing { return lastReports[clip.id] ?? .empty }
960	        guard let set = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey),
961	              let source = layerSource(of: clip),
962	              case .graphic(_, let hash, let frame, let propsJSON, let ctxJSON) = source
963	        else { return .empty }
964	        let key = [
965	            shared.name, revision, libraryVersion, hash, "\(graphic.width)×\(graphic.height)",
966	        ].joined(separator: "|")
967	        if let hit = reportMemo[key] {
968	            lastReports[clip.id] = hit
969	            return hit
970	        }
971	        var render: [GraphicDiagnostic] = []
972	        do {
973	            let drawn = try module.svg(
974	                frame: frame, propsJSON: propsJSON, ctxJSON: ctxJSON,
975	                budgetMs: GraphicRegistry.previewBudgetMs)
976	            render += drawn.warnings
977	            do {
978	                let raster = try set.library.rasterize(
979	                    drawn.svg, width: graphic.width, height: graphic.height)
980	                render += raster.warnings
981	            } catch {
982	                render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
983	            }
984	        } catch {
985	            render += GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
986	        }
987	        let report = GraphicClipReport(
988	            compile: module.compileWarnings, render: render, frame: frame)
989	        if reportMemo.count >= 64 { reportMemo.removeAll() }
990	        reportMemo[key] = report
991	        lastReports[clip.id] = report
992	        return report
993	    }
994	
995	    /// `clip`'s layer source in the recipe at its start, through
996	    /// `layerMemo`: `recipe(at:)` is asked only on a miss, and the memo is
997	    /// emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
998	    func layerSource(of clip: ClipSnapshot) -> RecipeSourceRef? {
999	        guard let project = binding.project else { return nil }
1000	        if project !== layerProject {
1001	            layerMemo = [:]
1002	            layerProject = project
1003	        }
1004	        if let hit = layerMemo[clip.id] { return hit }
1005	        guard let layer = project.recipe(at: clip.start)?.layers
1006	            .first(where: { $0.clip == clip.id })
1007	        else { return nil }
1008	        layerMemo[clip.id] = layer.source
1009	        return layer.source
1010	    }
1011	
1012	    /// Copies the module's file under a new name the person types, then
1013	    /// repoints the selected clips at it with `set_graphic {name}` — the
1014	    /// copy is not undoable (G-3), the repoint is one step. The MCP mirror is
1015	    /// `write_graphic` of the source under the new name, then `set_graphic`.
1016	    func duplicateAsNewGraphic(_ file: GraphicModuleFile, schema: [String: Any]?) {
1017	        guard let store = binding.document?.graphicStore else { return NSSound.beep() }
1018	        let suggestion = store.uniqueModuleName(file.name + "-copy")
1019	        let alert = NSAlert()
1020	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
1021	        alert.messageText = "Duplicate \(file.name).js as a new graphic"
1022	        alert.informativeText =
1023	            "The copy is written into the package's graphics/ folder and the selected clips "
1024	            + "are drawn by it. Writing the file cannot be undone; switching the clips can."
1025	        let field = NSTextField(string: suggestion)
1026	        field.frame = NSRect(x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: 24)
1027	        field.placeholderString = "Module name"
1028	        alert.accessoryView = field
1029	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Duplicate")
1030	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
1031	        alert.window.initialFirstResponder = field
1032	        guard alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
1033	        let name = field.stringValue.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
1034	        func refuse(_ sentence: String) {
1035	            NSAlert(error: NSError(
1036	                domain: "FrameJob", code: 1, userInfo: [NSLocalizedDescriptionKey: sentence]))
1037	                .runModal()
1038	        }
1039	        guard GraphicStore.isModuleName(name) else { return refuse(GraphicStore.nameSentence(name)) }
1040	        guard !store.holdsModule(named: name) else {
1041	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js already exists")
1042	        }
1043	        do {
1044	            try store.write(name: name, source: String(decoding: file.bytes, as: UTF8.self))
1045	        } catch {
1046	            return refuse("graphics/\(name).js could not be written: \(error.localizedDescription)")
1047	        }
1048	        store.rescan()
1049	        let clips = binding.graphicClips.map(\.id)
1050	        binding.apply(
1051	            "Duplicate Graphic",
1052	            clips.isEmpty ? [] : [.setGraphicRaw(clips: clips, patch: ["name": name], schema: schema)])
1053	    }
1054	}
1055	
1056	/// One diagnostic: "line L, column C — message", an error in the strong
1057	/// ink and a warning in the muted one. A click on it, or on its Open, opens
1058	/// the module in the editor; a folder row's button is Reveal instead.
1059	final class GraphicDiagnosticRow: NSView {
1060	    let diagnostic: GraphicDiagnostic
1061	    private let onOpen: () -> Void
1062	    let label = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
1063	
1064	    init(
1065	        _ d: GraphicDiagnostic, openTitle: String = "Open",
1066	        help: String = "Open the module in the editor", onOpen: @escaping () -> Void
1067	    ) {
1068	        diagnostic = d
1069	        self.onOpen = onOpen
1070	        super.init(frame: .zero)
1071	        var place = ""
1072	        if let line = d.line {
1073	            place = d.column.map { "line \(line), column \($0) — " } ?? "line \(line) — "
1074	        }
1075	        label.stringValue = place + d.message
1076	        label.font = DS.sans(11)
1077	        label.textColor = d.level == "error" ? DS.textStrong : DS.textMuted
1078	        label.isSelectable = false
1079	        label.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = 200
1080	        label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
1081	        let open = OptionButtonControl(
1082	            title: openTitle, action: { [weak self] in self?.onOpen() }, enabled: { true },
1083	            onEdit: {})
1084	        open.setContentHuggingPriority(.required, for: .horizontal)
1085	        let row = NSStackView(views: [label, open])
1086	        row.orientation = .horizontal
1087	        row.alignment = .top
1088	        row.spacing = 6
1089	        row.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
1090	        addSubview(row)
1091	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
1092	            row.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: topAnchor),
1093	            row.bottomAnchor.constraint(equalTo: bottomAnchor),
1094	            row.leadingAnchor.constraint(
1095	                equalTo: leadingAnchor, constant: InspectorMetrics.markGutter),
1096	            row.trailingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: trailingAnchor),
1097	        ])
1098	        toolTip = help
1099	    }
1100	
1101	    @available(*, unavailable)
1102	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
1103	        fatalError("GraphicDiagnosticRow does not support NSCoder")
1104	    }
1105	
1106	    override func mouseDown(with event: NSEvent) {
1107	        onOpen()
1108	    }
1109	}

1	// app/Sources/GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift — Insert ▸ Graphic… (spec
2	// §11 G-45): a sheet of three panes — the categories, the graphics of the
3	// chosen one, and a looping preview of the chosen graphic with its title and
4	// one-line description — over a message line and a bottom bar of Export… and
5	// From File… at the left and Cancel and Insert at the right.
6	//
7	// **What it lists is `GraphicCatalog.categories(for:)`**, read once when the
8	// sheet is made, in the order `list_graphics` answers. It opens on the first
9	// category's first graphic; Insert is disabled with no graphic chosen, and a
10	// double-click on a graphic is Insert.
11	//
12	// **No second implementation.** Insert is one call of the editor's body —
13	// `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` with the template's URL, or
14	// `insertProjectGraphic(named:grouped:)` for This Project — the bodies the
15	// old menu items called, which call `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift`
16	// as `insert_graphic` does. It runs inside the button's event, so `grouped:
17	// false` (`applyEdit`). A success dismisses the sheet; a throw beeps and
18	// shows the sentence word for word in `messageLabel`, and the sheet stays.
19	//
20	// **What follows the sheet starts in `viewDidDisappear`**, for
21	// `ReverseProgressSheetController`'s reason: a sheet dismissed a moment ago
22	// is still the window's `attachedSheet`. From File… only sets a flag and
23	// dismisses; the open panel is begun there, once the browser is down. And
24	// the preview's render thread is stopped there, so every way out — Cancel,
25	// Esc, Insert, From File… — stops it.
26	//
27	// **Opened after an import** (spec §11 G-47 (f)) with `select`: This Project
28	// and the graphic of that name are chosen, and `message` is put in the
29	// message line after the choice has cleared it.
30	//
31	// **Export…** (spec §11 G-46 (a)) is enabled when the chosen graphic
32	// compiles and no export is running. It opens a save panel as a sheet on the
33	// browser, which stays up; `exportChosen(to:)` builds a `GraphicPackageJob` on
34	// main and writes it on a `Thread` of `GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes`
35	// (QuickJS needs the stack), and the result or the refusal goes in the
36	// message line. No edit and no undo step.
37	
38	import AppKit
39	
40	final class GraphicBrowserSheetController: NSViewController, NSTableViewDataSource,
41	    NSTableViewDelegate
42	{
43	    /// Weak, like every sheet's back-reference.
44	    private weak var document: ProjectDocument?
45	    private weak var editor: EditorViewController?
46	    private let categories: [GraphicBrowserCategory]
47	    private let canvas: CanvasSnapshot
48	    private var fromFilePending = false
49	    /// The graphic to choose and the message to show at load (G-47 (f)).
50	    private let select: String?
51	    private let message: String?
52	    /// An export's thread is running; Export… stays disabled until it reports.
53	    private(set) var exporting = false
54	    /// The last export's thread, for the probe to see it finish.
55	    private(set) var exportThread: Thread?
56	
57	    private let categoryTable = NSTableView()
58	    private let graphicTable = NSTableView()
59	    private let previewView = NSImageView()
60	    private let titleLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
61	    private let descriptionLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
62	    private let messageLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
63	    private let insertButton: NSButton
64	    private let fromFileButton: NSButton
65	    private let exportButton: NSButton
66	
67	    /// The preview's loop; its thread starts with the first graphic shown.
68	    private(set) lazy var player = GraphicPreviewPlayer(canvas: canvas) { [weak self] image in
69	        self?.showFrame(image)
70	    }
71	
72	    private static let width: CGFloat = 920
73	    private static let paneHeight: CGFloat = 410
74	    private static let categoriesWidth: CGFloat = 180
75	    private static let graphicsWidth: CGFloat = 240
76	    private static let gap: CGFloat = 12
77	    private static let cellID = NSUserInterfaceItemIdentifier("graphicbrowser.cell")
78	
79	    init(
80	        document: ProjectDocument, editor: EditorViewController, select: String? = nil,
81	        message: String? = nil
82	    ) {
83	        self.document = document
84	        self.editor = editor
85	        self.select = select
86	        self.message = message
87	        self.categories = GraphicCatalog.categories(for: document)
88	        self.canvas = document.project.snapshot.canvas
89	        self.insertButton = StickerButton(title: "Insert", style: .primary, target: nil, action: nil)
90	        self.fromFileButton = StickerButton(
91	            title: "From File…", style: .secondary, target: nil, action: nil)
92	        self.exportButton = StickerButton(
93	            title: "Export…", style: .secondary, target: nil, action: nil)
94	        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
95	    }
96	
97	    @available(*, unavailable)
98	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
99	        fatalError("GraphicBrowserSheetController does not support NSCoder")
100	    }
101	
102	    // MARK: - Layout
103	
104	    override func loadView() {
105	        let contentWidth = Self.width - sheetInset * 2
106	        let previewWidth = contentWidth - Self.categoriesWidth - Self.graphicsWidth - Self.gap * 2
107	        configure(categoryTable, id: "graphicbrowser.categories")
108	        categoryTable.allowsEmptySelection = false
109	        configure(graphicTable, id: "graphicbrowser.graphics")
110	        graphicTable.target = self
111	        graphicTable.doubleAction = #selector(graphicDoubleClicked(_:))
112	
113	        // The well at the canvas's aspect ratio, as large as the column allows
114	        // with the title and description under it.
115	        let room = NSSize(width: previewWidth, height: Self.paneHeight - 56)
116	        let aspect = CGFloat(max(canvas.width, 1)) / CGFloat(max(canvas.height, 1))
117	        let well = aspect >= room.width / room.height
118	            ? NSSize(width: room.width, height: (room.width / aspect).rounded())
119	            : NSSize(width: (room.height * aspect).rounded(), height: room.height)
120	        previewView.imageScaling = .scaleProportionallyUpOrDown
121	        previewView.wantsLayer = true
122	        previewView.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.canvasVoid.cgColor
123	        previewView.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.preview")
124	        previewView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
125	        previewView.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.width).isActive = true
126	        previewView.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.height).isActive = true
127	
128	        titleLabel.font = DS.sans(13, weight: .bold)
129	        titleLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
130	        titleLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
131	        titleLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.title")
132	        descriptionLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
133	        descriptionLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
134	        descriptionLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
135	        descriptionLabel.maximumNumberOfLines = 1
136	        descriptionLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.description")
137	        // A plain view with every edge pinned, so nothing in the column is
138	        // left to a stack's low-priority guesses.
139	        let previewColumn = NSView()
140	        previewColumn.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
141	        for label in [titleLabel, descriptionLabel] {
142	            label.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
143	            label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
144	        }
145	        for piece in [previewView, titleLabel, descriptionLabel] { previewColumn.addSubview(piece) }
146	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
147	            previewColumn.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
148	            previewColumn.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight),
149	            previewView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.topAnchor),
150	            previewView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
151	            titleLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewView.bottomAnchor, constant: 10),
152	            descriptionLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: titleLabel.bottomAnchor, constant: 6),
153	        ] + [titleLabel, descriptionLabel].flatMap { label in
154	            [
155	                label.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
156	                label.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
157	            ]
158	        })
159	
160	        let panes = NSStackView(views: [
161	            scroll(categoryTable, width: Self.categoriesWidth),
162	            scroll(graphicTable, width: Self.graphicsWidth), previewColumn,
163	        ])
164	        panes.orientation = .horizontal
165	        panes.alignment = .top
166	        panes.spacing = Self.gap
167	        panes.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight).isActive = true
168	
169	        messageLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
170	        messageLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
171	        messageLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = contentWidth
172	        messageLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.message")
173	
174	        insertButton.target = self
175	        insertButton.action = #selector(insertClicked(_:))
176	        insertButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.insert")
177	        fromFileButton.target = self
178	        fromFileButton.action = #selector(fromFileClicked(_:))
179	        fromFileButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.fromFile")
180	        exportButton.target = self
181	        exportButton.action = #selector(exportClicked(_:))
182	        exportButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.export")
183	        let cancelButton = sheetCancelButton(target: self, action: #selector(cancelClicked(_:)))
184	        cancelButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.cancel")
185	        view = makeSheetView(
186	            title: "Insert Graphic", content: sheetColumn([panes, messageLabel]),
187	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(
188	                cancel: cancelButton, apply: insertButton, leading: [exportButton, fromFileButton]),
189	            width: Self.width)
190	
191	        categoryTable.reloadData()
192	        if !categories.isEmpty {
193	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: 0), byExtendingSelection: false)
194	        }
195	        categoryChanged()
196	        chooseSelected()
197	    }
198	
199	    /// `select` chosen under This Project, then `message` shown (G-47 (f)).
200	    private func chooseSelected() {
201	        if let select = select,
202	            let section = categories.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == GraphicCatalog.thisProject }),
203	            let row = categories[section].items.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == select })
204	        {
205	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: section), byExtendingSelection: false)
206	            categoryChanged()
207	            graphicTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: row), byExtendingSelection: false)

476	// app/Sources/GraphicPane.swift — the Clip tab's GRAPHIC sections (road map
477	// 10 §5j, G5a): Source (in `GraphicPane+Source.swift`), Properties from the
478	// module's schema (rows from `GraphicSchemaRows.swift`), Size and Timeline.
479	// With no action selected every write is `set_graphic`. With one selected, a
480	// Properties write — Reset's included — goes to the action's END with the
481	// module's current schema, one `set_action_end` naming `graphic.props.<key>`,
482	// except an `animate: false` prop's, which stays the clip's (spec §11 G-34
483	// (l), G-41 (d), G-42 (d)); Size and
484	// Timeline still write `set_graphic`, so their rows are ⊘. The core
485	// validates both.
486	//
487	// **Never shown itself**: like `ShapePane`, a factory `ClipPane` holds and
488	// calls when EVERY selected clip is a graphic clip.
489	//
490	// **Several graphic clips.** Source and Size always; Properties only when
491	// every clip is drawn by ONE module (one schema to build rows from, and the
492	// schema `set_graphic` needs), and Timeline only for one clip — its `in`
493	// and `length` are that clip's own. With different modules Source says so
494	// and names them (spec §11 G-15).
495	//
496	// **The schema is the registry's** (`GraphicRegistry.entry(named:for:)`,
497	// main only), the same read `AgentServer+Graphics.compiledModule` makes for
498	// the tool path. Nothing here rescans the store from an observer: `drain()`
499	// is not re-entrant (road map 10 §10.6 G3a).
500	
501	import AppKit
502	
503	extension InspectorBinding {
504	    /// The selected clips drawn by a module.
505	    var graphicClips: [ClipSnapshot] {
506	        clips.filter { clip in
507	            if case .graphic = clip.source { return clip.graphic != nil }
508	            return false
509	        }
510	    }
511	}

513	final class GraphicPane: InspectorPaneView {
514	    /// The report of each module/revision/library/frame hash/size seen, and
515	    /// the last report per clip — what a miss answers while a live gesture
516	    /// runs, so the signature holds still through a drag.
517	    var reportMemo: [String: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
518	    var lastReports: [UInt32: GraphicClipReport] = [:]
519	    /// The parsed schema of the last module asked, keyed "name|revision".
520	    var schemaMemo: (key: String, schema: GraphicSchema)?
521	    /// Each clip's recipe layer source under `layerProject`, the handle it
522	    /// was read from; emptied when the binding's project is another handle.
523	    weak var layerProject: ReelProject?
524	    var layerMemo: [UInt32: RecipeSourceRef] = [:]
525	
526	    /// Whether the graphic sections apply: they write `set_graphic`, which
527	    /// errors on any other kind, so a mixed selection gets none of them.
528	    var allGraphic: Bool {
529	        !binding.clips.isEmpty && binding.graphicClips.count == binding.clips.count
530	    }
531	
532	    /// The one module every selected graphic clip is drawn by.
533	    struct Shared {
534	        let name: String
535	        let file: GraphicModuleFile?
536	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?
537	    }
538	
539	    /// nil when the selection's modules differ (or it holds no graphic).
540	    func shared() -> Shared? {
541	        let names = Set(binding.graphicClips.compactMap { $0.graphic?.name })
542	        guard names.count == 1, let name = names.first else { return nil }
543	        let document = binding.document
544	        return Shared(
545	            name: name, file: document?.graphicStore?.module(named: name),
546	            entry: document.flatMap {
547	                GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: $0.recipeKey)
548	            })
549	    }
550	
551	    /// The compiled schema of `shared`, parsed in the module's order, and
552	    /// the registry's dictionary the ops carry. Parsed once per name and
553	    /// revision (`schemaMemo`).
554	    func schema(_ shared: Shared?) -> (schema: GraphicSchema, raw: [String: Any])? {
555	        guard let shared, case .compiled(let module, let revision, _, let raw)? = shared.entry
556	        else { return nil }
557	        let key = "\(shared.name)|\(revision)"
558	        if let memo = schemaMemo, memo.key == key { return (memo.schema, raw) }
559	        let parsed = GraphicSchema(describeJSON: module.describeJSON(), schema: raw)
560	        schemaMemo = (key, parsed)
561	        return (parsed, raw)
562	    }
563	
564	    /// The selection's stored props, merged; the first clip holding a key wins.
565	    func storedProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
566	        var merged: [String: GraphicPropValue] = [:]
567	        for clip in binding.graphicClips {
568	            merged.merge(clip.graphic?.props ?? [:]) { first, _ in first }
569	        }
570	        return merged
571	    }
572	
573	    /// The selected action's end props (G-34 (a)); none with no action
574	    /// selected. Its keys the schema lacks are the action's stale rows.
575	    func endProps() -> [String: GraphicPropValue] {
576	        binding.selectedAction?.end.graphic?.props ?? [:]
577	    }
578	
579	    /// The asset folder's file names, sorted.
580	    func assetNames() -> [String] {
581	        (binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.assets.map(\.name) ?? []).sorted()
582	    }
583	
584	    /// What the graphics folder's scan skipped or could not watch, in its own
585	    /// sentences — the Source section's folder rows (G-24 (b)).
586	    func folderWarnings() -> [String] {
587	        binding.document?.graphicStore?.scan.warnings ?? []
588	    }
589	
590	    /// The schema's entries whole (a default, bounds or options a row is
591	    /// built from), the stale keys (the clip's, then the selected action's
592	    /// end's, `actionStaleKeys`, a declared key no action may animate
593	    /// included, G-41), each asset popup's names (the selected end's
594	    /// included, G-42), the
595	    /// diagnostics' messages and the folder's warnings. Stored values, the
596	    /// revision and the playhead are NOT here: they are read fresh by
597	    /// `refresh()`.
598	    override var structureSignature: String {
599	        guard allGraphic else { return super.structureSignature + "|-" }
600	        let shared = self.shared()
601	        let parsed = schema(shared)
602	        let keys = parsed?.schema.entries.map { String(describing: $0) } ?? []
603	        let stale = GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: storedProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
604	        var messages = ["-", "-"]
605	        if let shared, let clip = binding.graphicClips.first, let document = binding.document {
606	            let version = GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)?.libraryVersion
607	            let report = self.report(for: clip, shared, libraryVersion: version ?? "")
608	            func spell(_ list: [GraphicDiagnostic]) -> String {
609	                list.map { "\($0.level):\($0.line ?? -1):\($0.column ?? -1):\($0.message)" }
610	                    .joined(separator: "¶")
611	            }
612	            messages = [spell(report.compile), spell(report.render)]
613	        }
614	        messages.append(folderWarnings().joined(separator: "¶"))
615	        return [
616	            super.structureSignature, shared?.name ?? "mixed", keys.joined(separator: ","),
617	            stale.joined(separator: ","), assetSignature(parsed?.schema),
618	            GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: endProps(), schema: parsed?.schema)
619	                .joined(separator: ","),
620	        ].joined(separator: "|") + "|" + messages.joined(separator: "|")
621	    }
622	
623	    /// Each asset entry's popup names, from the rows' own
624	    /// `GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames` call, the selected action's end's names
625	    /// counting (G-42 (d)): names joined by ",", entries by ";".
626	    private func assetSignature(_ schema: GraphicSchema?) -> String {
627	        let files = assetNames(), clips = binding.graphicClips
628	        return (schema?.entries ?? []).filter { $0.type == "asset" }.map {
629	            GraphicSchemaRows.assetNames(for: $0, files: files, clips: clips, end: endProps())
630	                .joined(separator: ",")
631	        }.joined(separator: ";")
632	    }

634	    // MARK: - Properties
635	
636	    /// One row per schema key in the module's order, then the stale keys,
637	    /// sorted, then — with an action selected — the end's own stale keys
638	    /// (G-34 (l), O2), a declared key whose entry is not `animatable` among
639	    /// them (G-41 (c)). With no compiled schema every stored key is stale.
640	    /// Reset nulls every stored key; with an action selected it writes each
641	    /// declared default through the rows' own split, into the END (an
642	    /// asset's `null` as `""`, G-42 (d)), an `animate: false` prop's (G-41
643	    /// (d)) onto the clip (O7). Its `differs` folds from the rows.
644	    func propertiesSection() -> InspectorSection {
645	        let binding = self.binding
646	        let shared = self.shared()
647	        let parsed = schema(shared)
648	        let clips = { binding.graphicClips }
649	        let assets = { [weak self] in self?.assetNames() ?? [] }
650	        var rows: [NSView] = parsed?.schema.entries.map {
651	            GraphicSchemaRows.row(
652	                $0, binding, clips: clips, schema: parsed?.raw ?? [:], assets: assets)
653	        } ?? []
654	        let stored = storedProps()
655	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.staleKeys(stored: stored, schema: parsed?.schema) {
656	            rows.append(
657	                GraphicSchemaRows.staleRow(
658	                    key: key, value: stored[key] ?? .null, binding, clips: clips))
659	        }
660	        let ends = endProps()
661	        let declared = Set(parsed?.schema.keys ?? [])
662	        for key in GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleKeys(end: ends, schema: parsed?.schema) {
663	            rows.append(
664	                GraphicSchemaRows.actionStaleRow(
665	                    key: key, value: ends[key] ?? .null, declared: declared.contains(key), binding))
666	        }
667	        let note: String?
668	        if parsed == nil {
669	            note = "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below."
670	        } else if parsed?.schema.entries.isEmpty == true {
671	            note = "The module declares no properties."
672	        } else {
673	            note = nil
674	        }
675	        let count = parsed?.schema.entries.count ?? 0
676	        return InspectorSection(
677	            id: "graphic.properties", title: "Properties",
678	            summary: { count == 1 ? "1 property" : "\(count) properties" },
679	            note: note.map { text -> () -> String? in { text } },
680	            reset: {
681	                if binding.selectedAction != nil {
682	                    let entries = parsed?.schema.entries ?? []
683	                    let defaults = Dictionary(
684	                        entries.map { ($0.key, $0.default) }, uniquingKeysWith: { first, _ in first })
685	                    binding.apply(
686	                        "Reset Graphic Properties",
687	                        binding.ops(
688	                            graphic: defaults, entries: entries, clips: clips(), schema: parsed?.raw))
689	                    return
690	                }
691	                let targets = clips()
692	                var keys = Set<String>()
693	                for clip in targets { keys.formUnion(clip.graphic?.props.keys.map { $0 } ?? []) }
694	                guard !keys.isEmpty else { return NSSound.beep() }
695	                binding.apply(
696	                    "Reset Graphic Properties",
697	                    [GraphicSchemaRows.op(
698	                        clips: targets,
699	                        props: Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: keys.map { ($0, NSNull()) }),
700	                        schema: parsed?.raw)])
701	            },
702	            defaultExpanded: true,
703	            rows: rows)
704	    }

748	            [

758	    /// The graphic's own timeline (G-9): In, read-only — the point
759	    /// `trim_start`, `roll` and `split` move — and Length, typed, which pins
760	    /// it; Follow Clip gives it back to the clip (`null`, which ends it at
761	    /// `in + duration`, G-9·c).
